Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! South African players are spreading out to take their respective field positions. Jamie Smith and Ben Duckett are the two openers for England. Nandre Burger to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

England replaced Sonny Baker with Saqib Mahmood to bring some experience in the bowling attack and did some justice to the changes. England did start well with the ball however, let things slip once the part-timers, Will Jacks and Jacob Bethell, entered into the attack. Brydon Carse, too, was among the runs. Jofra Archer was the pick of the lot as he bowled a much better second spell to end with four wickets. We all know how England performed in the first game, they'll be a bit nervous when they come out, while South Africa will be confident to start well. Stay tuned for the chase.

England had South Africa under a bit of pressure when they picked three wickets inside 20 overs. However, Matthew Breetzke and Tristan Stubbs put on a fighting partnership to put South Africa back on track and on the road for a big total. Matthew Breetzke nailed his shots and looked in fine touch throughout his innings. Tristan Stubbs struggled a bit but picked up the baton and started scoring at a higher rate once Matthew Breetzke departed. However, he was involved in a horrible run out with Dewald Brevis and was absolutely furious but Brevis made sure he does the heavy lifting as his 42 off 20 gave South Africa an extra push to go over 300.

A mammoth total from South Africa and they ride the confidence from their famous win in the first ODI. England so far have been beaten comprehensively in this series. England's thought of bowling first has backfired as South Africa have put on a big total.

South Africa were ruthless. Even they would have been a bit surprised with how England played but from South Africa’s point of view, it was a magical performance and would look to repeat it again to seal the series. Keshav Maharaj picked four wickets but it was Wiaan Mulder who broke the back of the hosts to plot the win. In the chase, as certain as it could be, Aiden Markram’s quick fire knock sealed the game. England’s batting approach will be in spotlight again. They have to show it was just a mere slip of form rather than an ongoing major problem. The Proteas on the other hand will be high on confidence to put on another thumping performance. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.

Hello and a warm welcome to everyone to the 2nd ODI between England and South Africa. We move from Headingley to the iconic Lord’s. The home team were outclassed, outplayed and outperformed by South Africa as they were bundled out for 131 runs inside 25 overs. From 82/3, they slipped to 131 with Jamie Smith’s fifty on top of the order the only highlight. England, from their recent hangover of the Hundred looked out of international form and were beaten thoroughly.
... MATCH DAY ...

England and South Africa head to Lord’s for the second ODI with the hosts under real pressure after being completely outplayed in the opener. England’s promising start at Headingley quickly turned into a nightmare as they crumbled to just 131 all out, with Jamie Smith’s fighting fifty the only bright spot in a batting display that looked rattled by South Africa’s disciplined attack. Sonny Baker’s tough debut added to their woes, and Harry Brook has a lot of things to ponder on. South Africa, on the other hand, were clinical with Keshav Maharaj’s four-wicket haul ripped through England’s middle order, and Aiden Markram’s explosive knock made light work of the chase, underlining their growing confidence. Looking beyond the first game, England’s explosive batting depth and aggressive mindset remain their biggest strengths, with Joe Root’s class, Ben Duckett’s stroke play, and Jos Buttler's fireworks providing stability, while the pace duo of Jofra Archer and Brydon Carse adds variety alongside Adil Rashid’s guile in the middle overs. However, their inconsistency under pressure and occasional struggles against quality spin remain areas of concern. South Africa boast a balanced outfit with an in-form top order led by Markram and Ryan Rickelton, all-round depth through Wiaan Mulder and Corbin Bosch, and a potent spin department anchored by Maharaj. The middle order wasn't even tested properly in the last game, and youngsters like Dewald Brevis and Tristan Stubbs will be itching to make their mark. Their challenge lies in maintaining composure if early wickets fall and ensuring their pace attack steps up on flatter tracks. With the Proteas looking to seal the series and the hosts desperate to bounce back, expect a fiercely contested clash at the home of cricket.
